surface_forms: le fils aîné du duc de Guermantes
son neveu le prince de Guermantes
La comtesse douairière d'Argencourt, née Seineport

appraisal_events.evidence: « Oriane de Guermantes qui est fine comme l'ambre, maligne comme un singe, douée pour tout... c'est le sang le plus pur, le plus vieux de France » ; « Mlle de Guermantes (Oriane), qui n'avait pas grand'chose, faisait plus parler de ses toilettes que toutes les Courvoisier réunies des leurs » ; « les Guermantes, en général, et particulièrement Oriane... esquissaient de charmantes révérences, vous tendaient la main comme à un camarade ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The whole Guermantes/Courvoisier comparison is organized to raise Oriane: her Tolstoy sally, her éclat without money, the dowager d'Argencourt's eulogy and the demi-intellectuals' worship, and the narrator's own credit to her for putting real warmth and spontaneity into 'le chic' against Courvoisier stiffness. The admirers are mocked, but the local elevation of Oriane over the rival clan is the dominant movement and is separately endorsed in the narrator's own voice.

appraisal_events.evidence: « c'était sur l'homme le plus riche et le mieux né... que le Génie de la famille avait porté le choix de l'intellectuelle, de la frondeuse, de l'évangélique Mme de Villeparisis » ; « Mme de Villeparisis eut chez elle toutes les nobles personnes dont elle se moquait » ; contrast: « le point de vue que défendait Saint-Loup quand il vivait avec Rachel... comportait... moins de mensonge que celui des demoiselles Guermantes en général ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The closing movement exposes Mme de Villeparisis's professed creed (birth and fortune count for nothing) as collapsing at once into the richest, best-born match, while her own social eclipse is noted; Saint-Loup is explicitly set above this hypocrisy for acting on his stated theories despite the family's horror.

status_effects.explanation: Locally she is the acknowledged centre of prestige: her word is carried from house to house, admired across and beyond the Guermantes world, and she eclipses the whole Courvoisier clan despite having less money.
Her meritocratic, anti-worldly principles are shown to be words only, overruled by the 'Génie de la famille' the moment a marriage is at stake.

The passage notes her difficult social crisis, the brilliant guests who no longer return, and society keeping her at a distance; her one crowded day is the wedding, after which the prince des Laumes cuts the cable.

He gains comparatively: the narrator credits him with less mendacity than the Guermantes young ladies because he acted in conformity with his professed theories, even at the cost of family disapproval.

ambiguities: The elevation of Oriane is transmitted through ironized admirers — the bas-bleu dowager comtesse d'Argencourt, the « faux hommes de lettres, ces demi-intellectuels » ready to die for a woman they will never meet — and the anecdote itself is flagged « Authentique ou non ». The narrator nonetheless credits the Guermantes and Oriane in his own voice with genuine amiability and spontaneity (and marks the parallel musical rehabilitation, not this one, as « peu justifiée »), so the reading taken is real elevation carried by mocked machinery rather than pure irony.

The hypocrisy charge in the closing paragraph falls on « les demoiselles Guermantes en général », which includes Oriane, so the same character the passage elevates is partly touched by the diminishment; Mme de Villeparisis is taken as the event's target because she is the named agent of the professed creed and of the marriage, and no countervailing negative effect is recorded for Oriane since it is not the passage's dominant local movement for her.
